concept.title: The holdout and the edit ratio
concept.shortdesc: The published TPU7x topics are the answer key. never reads them while drafting, and compares each draft with them afterward.

conbody.p: The sample DITA set (dita-corpus) holds four TPU generations. TPU7x is the newest, so it plays the new generation. While drafting, refuses to open any topic whose file name starts with tpu7x-, and the comparison topic that lists every generation. A test proves that no sentence from those topics reaches the model.

After drafting, the evaluator renders both topics as a reader sees them: keys resolved, reused notes expanded and draft comments left out. It splits each into word and punctuation tokens and counts the tokens a writer must insert, delete or replace to turn the draft into the published text. The edit ratio is that count divided by the length of the longer of the two. 0% means identical.
Only topics that have a sibling count toward the target. A stub for a concept that is new in the generation is shown with its edit ratio, but it is a set of questions, not a draft.
conbody.note: The published topics are adapted from Google's TPU7x page under CC BY 4.0. They are what the comparison uses; the page link on each draft opens Google's current page.
